$We first find the points of intersection of the curves& $y = \left|x^{2} - 9\right|$ and $y = 3$

which gives, \left|x^{2} - 9\right| = 3⇒ x^{2} - 9 = \pm 3$

Required area~$= 2{A}_{1} + 2{A}_{2}$~ ($∵$~The areas~${A}_{1}$~&~${A}_{2}$~are symmetrical about~$y -$~axis )

where~${A}_{1} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{6}\left[\left(9 - x^{2}\right) - \left(3\right)\right]dx$~

${A}_{1} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{6}\left(6 - x^{2}\right)dx= {6x - \dfrac{x3}{3}}_{0}^{6}$~$= 6\sqrt{6} - \dfrac{6\sqrt{6}}{3} = \dfrac{12\sqrt{6}}{3} = 4\sqrt{6}$

${A}_{2} = \mathop{∫}_{6}^{3}\left[3 - \left(9 - x^{2}\right)\right]dx + \mathop{∫}_{3}^{12}\left[3 - \left(x^{2} - 9\right)\right]dx$

$= {∫}_{6}^{3}\left(- 6 + x^{2}\right)dx + {∫}_{3}^{12}\left(12 - x^{2}\right)dx$

$= {- 6x + \dfrac{x3}{3}}_{6}^{3} + {12x - \dfrac{x3}{3}}_{3}^{12}$

$= \left(- 18 + 9\right) - \lleft(-6\sqrt{6} ++2\sqrt{6} )) + \lleft(12\sqrt{12} --4\sqrt{12}) - \left(36 - 9\right)$

$= - 36 + $4\sqrt{6} +++8\sqrt{12}

Hence, required area~$= 2{A}_{1} + 2{A}_{2}$

$= 2 \$lleft(4\sqrt{6}) +$2 \left(-36 + 4\sqrt{6} ++8\sqrt{12}\right)

=8\sqrt{6} -$72 + $8\sqrt{6} ++16\sqrt{12}$

$= 16\sqrt{6} ++16\sqrt{12} -$72$

$

$⇒ A = 16 + {\left[3x^{2} - \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]}_{4}^{6}$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{76}{3}$

$⇒ 12A = 304$

questions.q: Let $Y = Y ( X )$ be a curve lying in the first quadrant such that the area enclosed by the line $Y - y = Y^{'} ( x ) ( X - x )$ and the co-ordinate axes, where $( x, y )$ is any point on the curve, is always $\dfrac{- y^{2}}{2Y^{'} ( x )} + 1, Y^{'}\left(x\right) \ne 0$. If $Y ( 1 ) = 1$, then $12Y ( 2 )$ equals ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Plotting the line $Y - y = Y^{'} ( x ) ( X - x )$ we get,

Now, from the above diagram,

The area of the triangle formed will be,

$A = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{- y}{Y^{'} ( x )} + x\right) ( y - xY^{'}\left(x\right) )$

Now, according to the given condition we get,

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{- y}{Y^{'} ( x )} + x\right) ( y - xY^{'}\left(x\right) ) = \dfrac{- y^{2}}{2Y^{'} ( x )} + 1$

$⇒ \left(- y + xY^{'} ( x )\right)\left(y - xY^{'} ( x )\right) = - y^{2} + 2Y^{'} ( x )$

$⇒ - y^{2} + xyY^{'} ( x ) + xyY^{'} ( x ) - x^{2}\left[Y^{'} ( x )\right]2 = - y^{2} + 2Y^{'} ( x )$

$⇒ 2xy - x^{2}Y^{'} ( x ) = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2xy - 2}{x2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{2}{x}y = \dfrac{- 2}{x2}$

It is a linear differential equation,

Now, finding $IF = e^{- 2\ln x} = \dfrac{1}{x2}$

Now, the solution is given by,

$y \cdot \dfrac{1}{x2} = \dfrac{2}{3}x^{- 3} + c$

Given at $x = 1, y = 1$

$⇒ 1 = \dfrac{2}{3} + c ⇒ c = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Hence, the equation of the curve will be,

$Y = \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{X} + \dfrac{1}{3}X^{2}$

$⇒ 12Y ( 2 ) = \dfrac{5}{3} \times 12 = 20$
